old: Every SPARQL query has a hard 60-second deadline. A client that keeps sending past a 429 can be temporarily banned from the query service. The rate-limit page asks for 3 or fewer concurrent requests. Fifteen parallel REST reads sent with a User-Agent that names no contact answered 13 times 200 and twice 404, with no 429. A request with a generic library User-Agent (python-requests) answered 403 with a request to set a User-Agent, and 30 such parallel reads all answered 403.
new: Every SPARQL query has a hard 60-second deadline. A client that keeps sending past a 429 can be temporarily banned from the query service. The rate-limit page asks for 3 or fewer concurrent requests. Fifteen parallel REST reads sent with a User-Agent that names no contact answered 13 times 200 and twice 404, with no 429. A request with a generic library User-Agent (python-requests) answered 403 with a request to set a User-Agent, and 30 such parallel reads all answered 403. The per-minute ceilings are enforced by the REST gateway, an Envoy rate-limit service that keeps its counters in Redis, on the Action API and the REST API; the rate-limit FAQ says the request limits currently apply to those two APIs, and the query service is throttled by processing time instead. The gateway counts requests whose User-Agent names no contact per source address and requests whose User-Agent carries a contact per contact string. A 429 from the gateway carries Retry-After, the header x-envoy-ratelimited and the text "You are making too many requests to the API."
